en: Buddhavamsa 21:
The Lineage of Buddha Vipassī "After Phussa, moreover..."
The Fully Awakened One, the supreme among bipeds,
named Vipassī,
arose in the world as one possessed of vision.
Having shattered all ignorance,
he has attained supreme enlightenment;
now he turns the Wheel of Dhamma.
He departed for the city of Bandhumatī.
Having set the Wheel of Dhamma in motion,
the Leader awakened both [his parents].
It cannot be expressed by calculation;
there was a first realization.
Furthermore, O one of immeasurable fame,
There he proclaimed the Truth;
there was a second realization for eighty-four thousand beings.
Eighty-four thousand [monks] followed the Fully Enlightened One into homelessness;
having reached the monastery, for them—
The Visionary taught the Dhamma.
Having heard it from him as he spoke in every aspect, those who sat near him [attained realization].
Having reached the excellent Dhamma,
there was the third realization;
there were three assemblies.
Of Vipassi, the Great Seer;
of those whose taints are destroyed, who are stainless,
whose minds are at peace, and who are steadfast.
There was a first assembly of one hundred and sixty-eight thousand [monks];
of monks numbering one hundred thousand—
The second assembly took place;
the third assembly consisted of eighty thousand bhikkhus.
There, in the midst of the assembly of monks,
the Fully Awakened One shines forth pre-eminently.
At that time, I was he.
A Naga king of great psychic power,
named Atula,
possessed of merit and radiance.
Then, surrounded by many tens of millions of nāgas,
I proceeded while sounding celestial musical instruments.
I approached the eldest in the world.
Having approached the Fully Awakened One,
Vipassī, the Leader of the World;
Having invited the King of Dharma, who was adorned with all ornaments and whose nails were inlaid with jewels and pearls, [she offered him...]
I gave him a golden seat.
That Buddha, sitting in the midst of the Saṅgha, made this prediction concerning me:
“Ninety-one eons from now,
this one will become a Buddha.
There was a delightful city called Kapila;”
Having gone forth,
the Tathāgata exerted himself in striving and performed difficult austerities.
Having sat down at the foot of the Ajapāla tree, the Tathāgata there partook of the milk-rice.
He approached the Nerañjarā River;
on the bank of the Nerañjarā,
that Victor partook of the milk-rice.
By the prepared excellent path, he will approach the foot of the Bodhi tree;
then, having circumambulated it to the right, he will sit down upon the seat of enlightenment.
The unsurpassed one will reach the seat of enlightenment;
at the foot of the Assattha tree,
the one of great renown will awaken to perfect enlightenment.
His mother who gave him birth shall be named Māyā;
his father shall be named Suddhodana.
This one will become Gotama—
free from taints, devoid of passion,
with a peaceful mind, and composed.
Kolita and Upatissa shall be the foremost disciples;
the attendant named Ānanda—
I shall attend upon this Victor.
Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā shall be the foremost among his female disciples.
Taintless, free from passion,
with peaceful minds and concentrated,
they attained awakening to that Blessed One.
He is called Assattha.
Citta and Hatthāḷavaka shall be the foremost attendants.
And Nandamātā and Uttarā shall be the foremost among attendants;
his lifespan shall be one hundred years.
Of the illustrious Gotama.
Having heard these words,
…pe…
"We shall be present before him.
Having heard his words,
my heart became even more serene.
I resolved upon a further vow for the fulfillment of the ten perfections.
There was a city named Bandhumatī,
The kṣatriya was named Bandhuma;
the mother of the great sage Vipassī was named Bandhumatī.
For eight thousand years he lived the household life;
Nanda, Sunanda, and Sirima—
There were three supreme palaces.
Forty-three thousand women were beautifully adorned.
That woman was named Sudassanā,
and her son was named Samavattakkhandha.
Having seen four omens, [he departed].
He departed by means of a chariot;
for no less than eight months,
the Victor exerted himself in striving.
Being entreated by Brahmā, the virtuous Vipassī, the Leader of the World,
the Great Hero, set the Wheel of Dhamma in motion.
In the Deer Park, the Supreme among Men had Khaṇḍa and he named Tissa as his two chief disciples.
The attendant of the Great Seer Vipassi was named Asoka;
and there were also Canda and Candamitta.
were his chief female disciples;
the Bodhi tree of that Blessed One is called the Pāṭali.
The naga Punabbasumitta and Sirima and Uttarā were their chief supporters.
They were his chief attendants.
Vipassī, the Leader of the World, was eighty cubits in height.
His radiance streams forth for seventy thousand years, extending seven yojanas all around.
Such was the lifespan of the Buddha;
remaining for that long,
he delivered many people across.
He liberated many gods and humans from their bonds,
and he pointed out the path and the non-path.
Having shown the light to the remaining worldlings and taught the deathless state,
Having blazed like a mass of fire,
he has gone out together with his disciples;
possessing supreme psychic power and supreme merit.
The auspicious marks have also faded away;
all that has vanished—
surely all conditioned phenomena are empty.
The supreme Victor, the Buddha Vipassī,
attained Parinibbāna in the Sumittā Monastery;
right there stands his most excellent stupa.
“Rising seven yojanas high.
This is the nineteenth chapter concerning the lineage of the Blessed One Vipassī.
